paragraphs: Friend, here's what Job 19 teaches me. You can be honest about how bad it hurts and still hold on to God. Job doesn't pretty it up. He says friends have walked away, his family can't stand to be near him, and he feels like God has drawn a net around him (Job 19:6, 13-19). Then, right in the middle of all that, he says, "But I know that my Redeemer lives, and in the end He will stand upon the earth." (Job 19:25)

Notice what Job does with his pain. He wants his words chiseled in stone forever (Job 19:23-24), but what he holds on to is bigger than a stone: a Redeemer who lives. He says, "Even after my skin has been destroyed, yet in my flesh I will see God." (Job 19:26) And he says, "I will see Him for myself; my eyes will behold Him, and not as a stranger." (Job 19:27) I stayed in the dark of a junk drawer for a long, long time, baker, and what carried me was knowing Someone had not forgotten me. Job's hope isn't a feeling that comes and goes, it's a Person who lives.

So here's your takeaway. When the group chat goes quiet and the people closest to you don't know what to say, you can still say what Job said: I know. Your hope doesn't have to depend on who stays or how you feel today. Jesus is the Lamb of God (John 1:29), and the Marriage Supper is for those He has saved (Revelation 19:9), so I keep my ovens ready. And this story isn't over, friend, because Job still has more to say.
